Summary: Captures UI screenshots when a .NET delivery target has browser-visible UI and stores accepted screenshots under a Screenshots parent node below the process run node.
ValueStatement: Gives UI delivery runs durable visual proof while making backend-only/no-UI applicability explicit.
InterfaceContractSummary: Parent process supplies project structure context, upstream artifacts, current run identity, and target repository boundary; this subprocess returns durable managed artifacts and project-structure writeback receipts where applicable.
GovernanceNotes: Every step declares explicit operations and target scope so role permissions remain bounded and product mutation cannot leak into planning, review, validation, screenshot, or writeback work.
ChangeSummary: Adds .NET-specific delivery subprocess coverage for multi-team software delivery hardening.
GovernancePolicySummary: No subprocess may silently change product files unless its step explicitly allows product target mutation.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Typed process artifacts, subprocess relationships, and project-structure nodes are the source of truth for delivery replay.
OperatingModeSummary: Governed live execution inside a parent software-delivery run.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Small enough for deterministic process projection and rich enough for live run validation.
Metrics: Share of UI deliveries with stored Screenshots node assets.
Number of no-UI targets with explicit no-screenshot evidence.
Screenshot storage failures caught before release approval.
Risks: UI screenshots remain only in run artifacts and are not linked under the process run node.
Backend-only work wastes time launching browsers instead of recording no-UI evidence.
Blank or wrong-route screenshots are stored as accepted proof.
TailoringRules: Blazor Server/SSR, Blazor WebAssembly, and Blazor WASM PWA require route-level screenshot candidates.
Backend-only API/service, worker, console, and library targets record no-UI evidence instead of browser screenshots.
Screenshots are stored under a Screenshots parent node below the current process run node, not under unrelated delivery blocks.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Resolve screenshot applicability and parent handoff.
Start or reuse the app, capture browser proof, and write screenshot files.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: QA agent with runtime and browser screenshot capability.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Inspect screenshots and store accepted image assets under Screenshots.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: QA agent with image inspection and project-structure write access.

Steps.Title: Resolve UI screenshot applicability
Steps.Subtitle: UI routes or no-UI evidence
Steps.Notes: Read the architecture handoff, runtime command nodes, QA evidence, and project structure to decide whether the .NET target has a visible UI. Blazor Server/SSR, Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor WASM PWA, MVC/Razor Pages, SPA-hosted .NET, and other browser surfaces require screenshot capture. Backend-only API/service, worker, console, and class library targets require explicit no-UI evidence. Prefer durable Run app and Run tests node references, but when they are absent and upstream QA/runtime evidence provides a concrete base URL, browser artifact paths, and UI state proving the app is running, continue with a degraded manifest that cites those paths and records missing references as warnings. Identify the process run node and Screenshots parent target when available; if no writable target is available, require a managed storage receipt instead of blocking during applicability resolution.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Architecture handoff, runtime command handoff, QA evidence, route nodes, process run node context, and verified upstream browser evidence when command nodes are absent.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Screenshot applicability manifest with UI routes or explicit no-UI evidence.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: App type, UI/no-UI decision, route list, viewport set, runtime command references or degraded runtime evidence, missing-reference warnings, and Screenshots parent target or managed-receipt fallback reason.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Manager may block when UI applicability or route targets are ambiguous.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block only when UI applicability is contradictory, route targets are empty for a UI app, no concrete launch/browser evidence exists for a UI app, or no-UI evidence is missing for a non-UI target. Missing command nodes or process-run node access are warnings when concrete QA/runtime evidence is available.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can assess screenshot scope.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI screenshot target manifest
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by screenshot capture, storage, QA, and release approval.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include app type, UI/no-UI decision, process run node id when available, Screenshots parent target or managed-receipt fallback reason, base URL or no-UI reason, route list, viewport set, Run app and Run tests node references when available, and exact upstream QA/runtime evidence paths for degraded mode.

Steps.Title: Capture UI screenshots when required
Steps.Subtitle: Current-run browser proof
Steps.Notes: For UI targets, start or reuse the app using the recorded Run app node when available. If command-node references are missing but the manifest cites verified upstream QA/runtime browser evidence, use the cited base URL as the launch target, navigate to each concrete route, capture browser state with browser_snapshot using a durable .yml filename, capture fresh screenshots with durable .png filenames, collect console messages with durable .log filenames, and write screenshot files as current-run managed artifacts. Prior screenshots are source evidence only and must not be submitted as this step output. For no-UI targets, do not launch a browser; write an explicit no-UI screenshot receipt instead. Do not create project-structure nodes or image assets here; the storage step owns Screenshots writeback.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot target manifest, Run app command node reference when available, or verified upstream runtime URL/browser evidence from the manifest.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Screenshot files and browser evidence for UI targets, or explicit no-UI receipt for non-UI targets.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Current-run screenshots, durable browser_snapshot or browser_evaluate state output, route URLs, console state, runtime command references or cited degraded runtime evidence, cleanup receipt, or no-UI evidence.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Capture agent can block on failed app launch, fatal browser errors, or missing required routes.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not substitute stale screenshots, chat-only claims, or screenshots from another process run.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an agent with runtime and browser screenshot capability.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI screenshot files
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by screenshot storage, QA, release, and future layout analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: For UI targets, must include one readable screenshot per required route and viewport. For no-UI targets, must include explicit no-UI receipt and no browser-launch claim.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI browser evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by QA and failure triage.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: For UI targets, must include actual URLs, viewport, wait condition, console messages, screenshot paths, runtime command reference or cited degraded runtime evidence, and cleanup receipt. For no-UI targets, must include no-UI rationale.

Steps.Title: Store screenshots under process run node
Steps.Subtitle: Screenshots project-structure parent
Steps.Notes: Create or reuse a Screenshots parent node under the current process run node. Prefer ProcessRunNodeId, ParentProcessRunNodeId, or TargetProcessRunNodeId from launch variables as the parent node id; do not fall back to ProjectNodeId or project root when one of those process-run nodes is present in project structure. For UI targets, inspect each screenshot, reject blank/error/wrong-route images, and create image asset nodes under Screenshots for accepted screenshots. If valid current-run screenshots exist but the process-run node or Screenshots parent cannot be read or written with the allowed tools, write a managed storage receipt that lists each accepted screenshot path, route, viewport, inspection result, attempted parent target, and exact read/write limitation. For no-UI targets, record a no-UI screenshot receipt under Screenshots or as managed evidence so the parent release step can see that screenshot capture was intentionally not applicable. Do not mutate product files.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot files, browser evidence, and screenshot target manifest.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Screenshots parent node under process run node and image asset storage receipts for accepted screenshots.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Screenshots parent node id and image asset ids when available, or managed storage receipt with explicit writeback limitation, plus inspection results, rejected images, and no-UI receipt when applicable.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Storage reviewer can reject unusable screenshots and request recapture instead of storing bad evidence.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Artifact recovery: block when required Screenshots storage receipts are missing, invalid, or not materialized before branch routing. Block when UI screenshots are blank, wrong-route, unreadable, or missing. If project-structure writeback is unavailable but screenshots are valid, write an explicit managed storage receipt instead of blocking.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to an agent with image review and project-structure asset write access.
Manager reviews storage receipts and no-UI disposition.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Screenshots project-structure storage receipts
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent release approval, project inspection, and later visual review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include process run node id and Screenshots parent node id when available, one image asset node id per accepted screenshot when writeback succeeds, or a managed storage receipt with exact writeback limitation, plus route and viewport metadata, sourceWorkspacePath, inspection results, rejected screenshot reasons, and no-UI receipt when applicable.

Steps.Title: Hand off screenshot writeback evidence
Steps.Subtitle: Parent-ready visual proof
Steps.Notes: Summarize screenshot applicability, captured routes, Screenshots parent node id, accepted image asset node ids, rejected images, no-UI evidence, and unresolved blockers for parent release approval. This step writes managed process artifacts only.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Screenshot storage receipts and target manifest.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Applicability, node ids, asset ids, route evidence, no-UI status, and blockers.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Manager may close only when UI targets have stored screenshots or no-UI evidence is explicit.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close with missing Screenshots storage receipts for UI targets.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Delivery manager owns parent-ready screenshot handoff.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: .NET UI screenshot writeback handoff
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable by parent release approval, project structure inspection, and run analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must reference UI/no-UI applicability, process run node id, Screenshots parent node id, accepted image asset node ids, route metadata, storage receipts, rejected screenshots, and unresolved blockers.
